DATACAMP GUIDED PROJECT · PYTHON

Sleep Health & Lifestyle Analysis

A guided exercise using Python and pandas to compare sleep duration and quality across occupations, then measure the share of each BMI group recorded with insomnia.

374records in the supplied sample
5.9 hrslowest occupation average · Sales Representatives (n=2)
43.2%insomnia share in the Overweight group (64 of 148)

EXERCISE BRIEF

Explore sleep and lifestyle patterns

The DataCamp exercise frames the analysis around an anonymized dataset of average sleep and lifestyle metrics for 374 people. The questions focus on which occupation has the lowest average sleep duration and quality, plus the proportion of each BMI category with insomnia.

FINDINGS

The lowest averages came from a very small group

Sales Representatives had the lowest mean sleep duration (5.9 hours) and sleep quality (4/10). This occupation has only two records, so the result is highly sensitive to individual observations.

Insomnia appeared in 9 of 216 Normal BMI records (4.2%), 64 of 148 Overweight records (43.2%), and 4 of 10 Obese records (40.0%).

METHOD & LIMITATIONS

Simple grouped comparisons, read with care

  • Loaded and reviewed the supplied CSV with pandas.
  • Grouped records by occupation and compared mean sleep duration and quality.
  • Counted insomnia records within each BMI category and divided by the category total.
  • Results are descriptive patterns in this sample; they do not establish causation or clinical conclusions.
  • The Sales Representative (n=2) and Obese (n=10) groups are small, so their estimates should be treated cautiously.

PYTHON WALKTHROUGH

Read the analysis code

These are the three Python cells used in the guided exercise. Open a step to read or copy the code.

01 · Load and inspect the dataPython · pandas
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("sleep_health_data.csv", keep_default_na=False)
print(f"Rows: {len(df)} | Columns: {df.shape[1]}")
print("\nSleep disorder values:\n", df["Sleep Disorder"].value_counts().to_string())
02 · Compare sleep by occupationPython · pandas
occupation_summary = (
    df.groupby("Occupation", as_index=False)
      .agg(people=("Person ID", "count"),
           avg_sleep_hours=("Sleep Duration", "mean"),
           avg_sleep_quality=("Quality of Sleep", "mean"))
)

lowest_duration = occupation_summary.loc[occupation_summary["avg_sleep_hours"].idxmin()]
lowest_quality = occupation_summary.loc[occupation_summary["avg_sleep_quality"].idxmin()]
print(f"Lowest average sleep duration: {lowest_duration['Occupation']} — {lowest_duration['avg_sleep_hours']:.1f} hours (n={lowest_duration['people']})")
print(f"Lowest average sleep quality: {lowest_quality['Occupation']} — {lowest_quality['avg_sleep_quality']:.1f} / 10 (n={lowest_quality['people']})")
03 · Calculate insomnia share by BMI groupPython · pandas
bmi_summary = (
    df.assign(is_insomnia=df["Sleep Disorder"].eq("Insomnia"))
      .groupby("BMI Category", as_index=False)
      .agg(people=("Person ID", "count"),
           insomnia_cases=("is_insomnia", "sum"))
)
bmi_summary["insomnia_share_pct"] = (bmi_summary["insomnia_cases"] / bmi_summary["people"] * 100).round(1)
print(bmi_summary.to_string(index=False))
